meta.title: GLP-1 Agonists Are Associated With a Significant Reduction in Breast Cancer Incidence in Women.
meta.abstract:
Purpose

Excess weight is a key modifiable risk factor for breast cancer. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1) promote weight loss and improve metabolic health, but their effect on breast cancer risk remains unclear.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cohort study from January 1, 2022, to June 30, 2025, using electronic health records. We identified 217,624 unique women who underwent breast imaging; restricting to ages 45-80 years with a BMI ≥25 and a documented imaging outcome (n = 111,646; median age 61 years). The primary outcome was breast cancer detection. GLP-1 use was defined as a first prescription before the examination date and assessed in relation to race, ethnicity, age, and type 2 diabetes. To address potential confounding between these covariates and GLP-1 exposure, we performed one-to-one, case-control matching using propensity scores on the basis of age, race, ethnicity, highest BMI, breast density, and history of type 2 diabetes. The propensity matching to the GLP-1 use group was performed using the greedy nearest neighbor approach.

Results

GLP-1 exposure was associated with a lower incidence of breast cancer (odds ratio [OR], 0.649 [95% CI, 0.569 to 0.741]; P < .0001). In the matched logistic regression (30,528 observations; 600 cancer cases), GLP-1 exposure was associated with a lower breast cancer incidence (OR, 0.695 [95% CI, 0.590 to 0.819]; P < .0001).

Conclusion

In this large observational study of women undergoing breast imaging at a major academic center and affiliated sites, GLP-1 treatment was associated with a lower incidence of breast cancer, independent of age, race, ethnicity, BMI, breast density, and diabetes. The findings support the need for prospective trials investigating GLP-1 agonists for breast cancer prevention.

domains.name: Confounding
domains.direction_justification: In the matched dataset (Table A2), non-GLP-1 controls had a higher prevalence of prior breast cancer history (7.8%, n=1,197) compared to GLP-1 users (5.9%, n=907), despite prior breast cancer being a major determinant of future cancer risk. In addition, key breast cancer confounders including parity, family history of breast cancer, duration of diabetes, and hormone replacement therapy were unmeasured and omitted from matching.

findings.title: Imbalance in prior history of breast cancer
findings.mechanism: Prior breast cancer history substantially increases risk of cancer detection or recurrence; having a higher baseline rate in the unexposed matched group creates an artificial protective association for the exposed group.
evidence: Table A2: History of breast cancer was 7.8% (1,197/15,264) in the No GLP-1 matched group vs 5.9% (907/15,264) in the GLP-1 matched group.

findings.title: Unmeasured reproductive and lifestyle confounders
findings.mechanism: Omission of known oncogenic risk factors (parity, age at menarche/menopause, HRT use, family history, and duration of type 2 diabetes) leaves substantial residual confounding.
evidence: Propensity score matching variables were restricted only to age, race, ethnicity, highest BMI, breast density, and any ICD code for type 2 diabetes (Methods, p. 1343).

findings.title: Baseline paradox: worse starting position, better outcome
findings.mechanism: indication bias / confounding by indication; differential detection / screening mammography timing; unmeasured healthy user bias among those prescribed newer antidiabetic/weight-loss medications; residual confounding from unadjusted baseline breast cancer history and comorbidity trajectories

domains.name: Measurement of the exposure
domains.direction_justification: Defining exposure as any single prescription before the imaging examination across a short 3.5-year study window (2022 to 2025) without requiring minimum exposure duration, cumulative dose, or biological latency allows reverse causality and immortal time / protopathic bias to exaggerate a protective effect (matched OR 0.695).

findings.title: Absence of latency and cumulative dose requirement
findings.mechanism: Breast carcinogenesis takes years to develop; observing a 30.5% reduction in breast cancer detection over a 3.5-year observation period without requiring minimum exposure duration implies that short-term or transient exposure is misclassified as causally protective.
evidence: GLP-1 use was defined as a first prescription before the examination date without duration or dosage thresholds (Methods, p. 1342; Discussion, p. 1347).

findings.title: Potential out-of-system exposure misclassification
findings.mechanism: Prescriptions filled outside the health system or through compounding pharmacies were not captured in EHR records.
evidence: Authors acknowledge potential ascertainment bias from uncaptured outside prescriptions (Discussion, p. 1347).

findings.title: Prevalent-user design without inception cohort or washout
findings.mechanism: Defining exposure as 'any prior or current use' without a baseline lookback/washout period admits prevalent survivors of early treatment, creating healthy user and depletion-of-susceptibles bias that inflates protective associations.
evidence: GLP-1 agonist use was defined as a first prescription before the examination date
associated with any prior or current use of GLP-1 agonist
We also did not require a minimum duration of therapy

findings.title: Immortal and event-free time in exposure classification
findings.mechanism: Classifying patients into the exposed cohort conditional on receiving a prescription prior to an index breast imaging examination requires patients to survive without a prior terminal event up to the imaging date.
evidence: GLP-1 agonist use was defined as a first prescription before the examination date
The primary outcome was a malignant breast pathology diagnosis during the study period.

findings.title: Absence of induction/lag period and insufficient follow-up for tumor latency
findings.mechanism: Breast neoplasms take years to develop; without a lag window to exclude cancers initiated before exposure, and with a total study duration of only 3.5 years, the observed reduction cannot plausibly reflect biological chemoprevention of cancer initiation.
evidence: retrospective cohort study from January 1, 2022, to June 30, 2025
We also did not require a minimum duration of therapy, because exposure is not definitely related to dose

domains.name: Selection of participants into the study
domains.direction_justification: Restricting the cohort strictly to women who underwent breast imaging and had a documented imaging outcome (111,646 out of 217,624 screened) induces collider stratification bias, as GLP-1 users experience differential clinical contact and screening surveillance compared to non-users.

findings.title: Collider conditioning on breast imaging participation
findings.mechanism: Conditioning inclusion on having undergone breast imaging within the health system during the study period selects for healthcare-seeking behavior, which correlates with both GLP-1 prescription and diagnostic scrutiny.
evidence: Cohort restricted from 217,624 unique women undergoing imaging to 111,646 women aged 45-80 with BMI >= 25 and documented imaging outcome (Figure 1, p. 1343).

domains.name: Post-exposure interventions
domains.direction_justification: Differential post-prescription clinical management, weight loss interventions (e.g., bariatric surgery), and concurrent antidiabetic therapy adjustments during the follow-up window were not accounted for.

findings.title: Untracked concomitant therapies and lifestyle changes
findings.mechanism: Co-interventions initiated after GLP-1 prescription (such as concurrent lifestyle programs or metformin/SGLT2i adjustments) could independently alter cancer risk.
evidence: No post-baseline treatment trajectories or co-medication records were tracked in the matched analysis.

domains.name: Missing data
domains.direction_justification: Exclusions were based on predefined objective eligibility criteria (age 45-80, BMI >= 25, documented imaging outcome), and matched analyses utilized complete cases (30,528 observations in 15,264 pairs).

findings.title: Exclusion for undocumented imaging outcomes or BMI < 25
findings.mechanism: A total of 54,799 women were excluded due to BMI < 25 or missing imaging outcomes from the age-eligible cohort of 166,445.
evidence: Figure 1: 54,799 excluded at the BMI/outcome stage leaving 111,646 in the full analysis set.

domains.name: Measurement of the outcome
domains.direction_justification: Breast cancer diagnosis was established via objective histopathology records across health system encounters (Table 1, Table 2).

findings.title: Histopathologically confirmed malignant diagnosis
findings.mechanism: Malignant breast pathology diagnoses were systematically documented through EHR pathology reports, minimizing diagnostic misclassification.
evidence: Matched set recorded 600 verified cancer cases (247 in GLP-1 vs 353 in No GLP-1; Table 2, p. 1345).

domains.name: Selection of the reported result
domains.direction_justification: Primary crude and matched analyses, along with complete contingency tables and subgroup breakdowns (diabetes, race), were transparently reported.

findings.title: Consistent presentation of matched and stratified analyses
findings.mechanism: Results were presented across both unmatched (OR 0.649, 95% CI 0.569 to 0.741) and matched models (OR 0.695, 95% CI 0.590 to 0.819), alongside subgroup tables.
evidence: Table 3, Table 4, Table 5, and Appendix Tables A1-A3 provide full contingency data and effect estimates.

overall.summary: McDonald et al. report that GLP-1 receptor agonist exposure is associated with a lower incidence of breast cancer among overweight/obese women undergoing breast imaging (matched OR 0.695 [95% CI, 0.590 to 0.819]; ARR 0.69%, NNT 144). However, the study carries a high risk of bias that threatens its causal conclusions. Crucially, matched controls had a higher prevalence of prior breast cancer history (7.8% vs 5.9%), which was omitted from matching alongside key reproductive/hormonal confounders. Furthermore, exposure was defined as any single prescription documented prior to imaging across a short 3.5-year observation period without latency or cumulative duration thresholds, inducing protopathic misclassification and collider selection bias in a cohort restricted to women receiving breast imaging.

baseline_comparability.summary: GLP-1 users had markedly worse metabolic risk and higher comorbidity (severe obesity, diabetes, renal/heart disease, Charlson scores) but were younger, had lower breast density, and lower prior breast cancer history. Although matching balanced demographic and diabetes covariates, unmeasured and residual comorbidity differences persisted while favorable baseline density and breast cancer history favoured the exposed cohort.

immortal_time.why: Exposure was defined retrospectively as any prescription occurring before the imaging examination date; patients in the GLP-1 group had to remain alive and cancer-free until the imaging encounter to be categorized and evaluated, conferring immortal/event-free time prior to the exam.

time_related_biases.summary: The study uses an 'any prior or current use' exposure definition without an inception cohort, washout, or lag window across a 3.5-year calendar period, linking historical prescriptions directly to cross-sectional imaging findings. These compounded time-related defects (prevalent-user bias, immortal/event-free time, and follow-up far shorter than breast cancer latency) strongly bias results away from the null toward an artificial protective association.
